guide.title: CBRNE & Terrorism Response
guide.lead: Chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive events start the same way: several people sick or hurt at once, at one place. Think of a deliberate attack, expect a second device, stay out until police say it's safe, and treat the agent you can recognise.

sections.title: Suspect an attack when
items: Many casualties with the same signs at once
Unexplained odours, mists, powders or dead animals
An explosion at a crowded or symbolic place

steps.title: Stage
steps.text: Out of sight, upwind, away from vehicles and bins; police clear the area for secondary devices.

steps.title: Enter with protection
steps.text: In a warm zone only with police escort (rescue task force).

steps.title: Stop bleeding first
steps.text: Tourniquets, packing, airway; move casualties out fast.

steps.title: Blast injuries
steps.text: Primary (lungs, ears, bowel), secondary (fragments), tertiary (thrown), quaternary (burns, crush).

sections.title: Chemical agents
rows: SLUDGEM, pinpoint pupils, wheeze, twitching, seizures
Atropine 2–6 mg IM/IV, repeat every 5 minutes until secretions dry; pralidoxime; midazolam or diazepam for seizures
Chlorine: immediate burning and cough. Phosgene: mild, then lung oedema hours later
Rest, oxygen, observe; anyone exposed to phosgene to hospital
Painless at first; redness and blisters hours later; eyes and lungs
notes: Auto-injector kits (DuoDote and similar) hold atropine 2.1 mg and pralidoxime 600 mg; benzodiazepines are separate.

sections.title: Biological agents
rows: Flu-like illness, then shock and a widened mediastinum
Fever, then a rash densest on the face and limbs, all lesions at the same stage
notes: Chickenpox lesions appear in crops at different stages and cluster on the trunk.

figures.alt: Two body outlines comparing rashes: smallpox densest on face and limbs with all lesions alike, chickenpox mainly on the trunk with lesions at different stages.

sections.title: Radiological and nuclear
items: Treat injuries first: contamination is rarely immediately dangerous to you
Strip and wash; survey if equipment is available

items.label: Bradycardia
items.sub: Nerve agents slow the heart: atropine.

quiz.q: Many people drooling, tearing, incontinent, with pinpoint pupils after a release. Likely agent and treatment?
options: Nerve agent (sarin): decontaminate, atropine and pralidoxime

quiz.q: Metal-plating worker: sudden headache, breathlessness, confusion, seizure, flushed skin. Treatment?
quiz.explanation: Cyanide is used in metal plating.

quiz.q: Market explosion; police haven't cleared the scene; a woman with a leg amputation lies near the blast site. You:
options: Stage safely until police clear the area or escort you in
Smallpox: densest on face and limbs, all lesions at the same stage
Smallpox only on palms and soles
quiz.explanation: Chickenpox: crops at different stages, mainly on the trunk.

quiz.q: Endpoint for atropine in nerve agent poisoning:
options: Drying of bronchial secretions and easier breathing

quiz.q: Phosgene exposure: mild cough now, feels fine. You:
options: Transport and observe: lung oedema can develop hours later

quiz.q: Is inhalational anthrax spread person to person?

options: Little at first; redness and blisters hours later

flashcards.question: SLUDGEM
flashcards.answer: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI upset, Emesis, Miosis: nerve agents and organophosphates.

flashcards.question: Nerve agent auto-injector kits
flashcards.answer: Atropine 2.1 mg and pralidoxime 600 mg (DuoDote and similar; the older Mark I kit was the same pair). Benzodiazepine separately for seizures.

flashcards.question: Mustard (blister agent)
flashcards.answer: Delayed: redness and blisters hours after exposure; eyes and lungs too. Decontaminate quickly even if no symptoms.

flashcards.question: Hydroxocobalamin
flashcards.answer: Cyanide antidote: 5 g IV over 15 minutes. Turns skin and urine red for days.

flashcards.question: Chlorine vs phosgene
flashcards.answer: Chlorine: immediate burning, cough, bleach smell. Phosgene: mild at first, then lung oedema hours later – rest and observe.

flashcards.question: Anthrax forms
flashcards.answer: Cutaneous (painless black eschar), inhalational (most lethal: flu-like then shock), gastrointestinal. Not contagious person to person.

critical.scenario: Community centre: about 30 people suddenly drooling, tearing, vomiting, incontinent, some twitching and seizing. Your partner heads inside with the kit.
critical.question: First action and sequence?

options.t: Stop your partner; stay upwind outside, declare a chemical mass-casualty incident, call hazmat, protected staff decontaminate, then atropine and pralidoxime and seizure control
Transport the first five without decontamination

critical.explanation: Nerve agents kill by secretions and respiratory failure: atropine until dry.
critical.kpi: Recognizes a nerve agent incident and protects responders

critical.scenario: A family across two households has fever, severe headache, aches and cough over 24 hours; the father is coughing blood and hypoxic. Similar calls are coming in.
critical.question: Suspicion and precautions?

options.t: Possible pneumonic plague (or another biological agent): masks for patients, N95, gown, gloves and eye protection for you, oxygen, notify hospital and public health

options.f: Clusters with bloody sputum are a red flag.

critical.explanation: Early public health notification saves lives.
critical.kpi: Recognizes a possible bioterrorism cluster and applies precautions

critical.scenario: Small bin explosion at a public event: a 9-year-old has a deep bleeding thigh wound and a white powder on his clothes. Police are still checking the area.
critical.question: How do you balance the risks?

options.t: Treat him where police allow: pressure or a tourniquet for the bleeding, remove the powdered clothing and bag it, protect yourself, notify hazmat and hospital
Enter the blast area for other victims

critical.explanation: Life-saving care and gross decontamination happen together.
critical.kpi: Balances hemorrhage control, contamination and scene safety
